_comment: Compliance Claw Slack app manifest — import this, do not assemble scopes by hand.
api.slack.com/apps/new -> Create New App -> From a manifest -> pick your
workspace -> paste this file -> Next -> Create.
Then, in the app you just created:
Basic Information -> App-Level Tokens -> Generate Token and Scopes
add connections:write, save, copy the token -> SLACK_APP_TOKEN in .env
Install App -> Install to Workspace
copy the Bot User OAuth Token       -> SLACK_BOT_TOKEN in .env
Invite the bot to one channel, copy that channel's ID (right-click ->
Copy link; the C... at the end of the URL) -> SLACK_CHANNEL_ID in .env
This is upstream's MINIMAL socket-mode scope set: 12 bot scopes instead of the
recommended 23. The 11 dropped are emoji:read, files:read, files:write,
mpim:history, mpim:read, mpim:write, pins:read, pins:write, reactions:read,
reactions:write and usergroups:read. Compliance Claw needs none of them: it
answers mentions in one allowlisted channel and reads repositories from a
local read-only mount.
The im:* scopes remain because they are part of upstream's supported minimal
set, but DMs are CLOSED at the OpenClaw layer by channels.slack.dmPolicy:
"disabled" (scripts/slack-channel.patch.json5). Granted-but-unused is stated
here rather than hidden — see SECURITY.md.
socket_mode_enabled means the gateway dials OUT to slack.com. There is no
request_url and no public endpoint, so the gateway port stays loopback-only.
The /claw slash command is declared but INERT unless an operator sets
channels.slack.commands.native: true. Mentions are the supported path here.
Slack ignores unknown top-level keys such as this one on import.
